outcome: mode of delivery (cesarean section, vaginal operative, spontaneous delivery)
cohort: The study assessed 1,202,557 deliveries in Hesse, Germany, between 1990 and 2012, with a focus on a subgroup of 26,761 deliveries subsequent to infertility treatment.
finding: A continuous and significant increase of cesarean section rates (from 41.3% in 1990 to 55.9% in 2012) and a converse reduction of vaginal deliveries were observed in parturients subsequent to infertility treatment in Hesse, Germany.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean section in parturients subsequent to infertility treatment continuously rose over 23 years, eventually exceeding vaginal deliveries (51.2% CS vs 48.8% vaginal) for the first time in Hesse.
